scenes.headline: How a giant hash table feeds a language model
scenes.sub: Tinfield 1, and the engram table inside its Qwen base.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Nutmeg! Tinfield 1 carries a fifty-one-billion-parameter hash table. Here's what it is, and why a token barely touches it.

scenes.label: What's in the download
scenes.text: Tinfield 1 is Qwen3.8-Flash-Next with its attention retrained: 1.85% of the weights moved. The biggest single piece is a hashed n-gram table.
scenes.say: Tinfield 1 is Qwen3.8-Flash-Next with its attention retrained: one point eight five percent of the weights. Its biggest piece is a hashed n-gram table.

scenes.title: Where the change is, and where the table plugs in

steps.say: A token climbs through forty-eight layers of attention and a mixture of five hundred and twelve experts.
The fine-tune moved every attention projection, and nothing else.

steps.note: byte for byte the base model
steps.say: All five hundred and twelve experts, in all forty-eight layers, are byte for byte the base model.
And at layer two, one extra input arrives: a row from the engram table, which is Qwen's, and also unchanged.
Take the last two or three token ids, and hash them with a polynomial of three large multipliers.
Reduce that hash modulo sixteen different primes, each just above twenty million. Sixteen heads, sixteen unrelated collision patterns.
Each head picks one row of a hundred and sixty numbers from its own slice of the table.
At layer two, one extra input arrives: a row from the engram table, which is Qwen's, and unchanged.

scenes.title: Why sixteen primes and not one table

left.title: One huge table
items: Two n-grams that collide stay confused, permanently
Nothing to average the collision away
left.say: With one huge table, two n-grams that land on the same row are confused forever.

right.title: Sixteen prime-sized heads
items: A collision under one prime almost never repeats under another
Concatenating sixteen rows averages the noise out
right.say: With sixteen prime-sized heads, a collision under one prime almost never repeats under another, so the noise averages out.

scenes.label: values a token reads, out of 51.2 billion in the table
scenes.note: a gather of about 5 KB, with no matrix multiply attached
scenes.say: A token reads two thousand five hundred and sixty values out of fifty-one billion. About five kilobytes, and no matrix multiply.

scenes.text: Embeddings scale by lookup, not by matmul. That is why the 26.8 GiB table can stay memory-mapped on the CPU.
scenes.say: So embeddings scale by lookup, not by matrix multiply. That's why the table can stay memory-mapped on the CPU side.

recap: Tinfield 1 retrained attention: 1.85% of the weights
The engram table is a hashed n-gram embedding
Sixteen prime moduli average collisions away
scenes.say: To recap: retrained attention, and a hashed n-gram table read through sixteen primes.
